title: Bag-out stoppage with unresponsive or out-of-sequence AGVs
user_facing_summary: Use this path when automated bag-out stops or progresses only partially and site personnel report that an AGV is not moving, a robot may be out of sequence, or a related HMI shows a fault.
playbook_goal: Determine whether the bag-out stoppage is associated with an abnormal AGV, pairing or sequence state, or an HMI-visible task or tote condition; apply only source-supported authorized recovery direction; and confirm that AGVs and bag-out remain functional.
observed_entry_symptoms: Automated bag-out stops after sorting or starts and then stops before completion.
Manual bagging out is required because the automated process does not progress.
One or more AGVs or robots appear not to be moving.
The site reports that a robot may be out of sequence or out of position.
An HMI associated with the hospital area shows a fault or a task-related condition.
negative_or_absent_signals: No stack-light fault was reported during one bag-out observation.
The exact AGV identifier, active error, task state, and decisive recovery action were not consistently readable or isolated.
The source does not confirm that the HMI update or stuck-task recovery process was completed.
support_user_language_examples: The hospital HMI has a fault
tentative_internal_patterns: Possible AGV sequence, pairing, roster, or position inconsistency.
Possible stuck task or tote association condition visible on an HMI.
Possible AGV inactivity or active-error condition.
Possible prior robot removal or replacement without a corresponding replacement in the operating sequence.
internal_pattern_notes: These are tentative patterns from the source, not confirmed diagnoses. The customer and support team suspected an out-of-sequence robot; an AGV was reported inactive for three hours; HMI evidence referenced a stuck task; and support discussed removing and adding AGV pairs. The source does not isolate which condition caused the stoppage.
confidence_reason: The packet contains a clear observable symptom, repeated AGV-related troubleshooting observations, source-supported pairing and sequence recovery direction, HMI fault evidence, and a customer-confirmed recovery state. However, the exact fault, decisive action, and complete diagnostic evidence are incomplete or ambiguous.
